messages:
Isha (Customer Success): FYI Acme reports structured-json streaming response gets truncated mid-object and their parser throws. route: /v1/generate-stream, model: redwood-7b, request_id: req_0a1b2c, happened ~2026-03-15T14:12:02Z. They pasted the tail: '... \"items\": [ {\"id\": \"a1\", \"value\": \"foo\" },' then connection reset. They suspect their corporate proxy.
Maya (Support): Do we have the raw server-side logs for req_0a1b2c? Any upstream/errors or proxy remote addr? If possible ask customer for exact curl/fetch they used (headers).
Isha (Customer Success): Customer sent this snippet they use to consume SSE: ```js
fetch('https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate-stream', {
  method: 'POST',
  headers: { 'Authorization': 'Bearer x', 'Accept': 'text/event-stream', 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
  body: JSON.stringify(payload)
}).then(r => { const reader = r.body.getReader(); // then they decode chunks and JSON.parse on assembled buffer
});
```
They get JSONDecodeError: "Expecting value" when parser hits the truncated buffer. They say it only happens when going through their proxy appliance.
Samir (SRE): Ok — two hypotheses: 1) proxy is closing the socket mid-stream (timeout or max buffer) 2) an intermediary rewrites or buffers and drops trailing chunk markers. Can we check ingress logs around that window? grep request_id=req_0a1b2c in router/nginx access + error logs and in the sse-gateway. Also check if connection was HTTP/2 -> HTTP/1.1 translation in their path.
Alex P (Eng): For streaming structured JSON, our runtime streams partial tokens. If a client concatenates raw bytes and JSON.parse only at the end, an early socket close yields partial JSON. For robustness we should recommend a framing strategy to customers: either send newline-delimited JSON events (one complete JSON per SSE data event) or include explicit \"finished\":true event. We can't change customer parser, but can provide guidance and a short repro to test proxy behavior.
Maya (Support): Isha — can you ask for the customer's full response headers for that request (they can paste the first few KB of the stream as hex or base64). Also request the proxy logs showing connection close.
Isha (Customer Success): They attached partial response headers: ```
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Content-Type: text/event-stream
Transfer-Encoding: chunked
Cache-Control: no-cache
X-Request-Id: req_0a1b2c

# then data: event: message
data: { \"items\": [ {\"id\":\"a1\",\"value\":\"foo\"},
data: { \"items\": [ {\"id\":\"a2\",\"value\":\"bar\"},
# connection reset happened here
```
They also sent a proxy log line: `proxy-01 2026-03-15T14:12:05 upstream prematurely closed connection while reading response`
Samir (SRE): That upstream error points to the proxy cutting the socket. Possible triggers: proxy idle timeout, max response buffer, or antivirus/splitting large streaming responses. Ask them to temporarily bypass the proxy or increase timeout to confirm. Meanwhile we should search our gateway for any process OOM/crash around that time.
Alex P (Eng): Quick internal repro command to simulate: ```bash
# emulate long SSE with chunked json pieces
python - <<'PY'
import time,sys
print('HTTP/1.1 200 OK\r\nContent-Type: text/event-stream\r\nTransfer-Encoding: chunked\r\n\r\n', end='')
for i in range(3):
  sys.stdout.write(f"data: {\"items\": [{{\"id\": \"{i}\", \"val\": \"x\"}} ,}\n")
  sys.stdout.flush(); time.sleep(0.8)
PY
```
Consume with curl and kill the client mid-stream to mimic proxy close. If parser fails reproducibly, it's client-side fragility.
Maya (Support): Created internal ticket SUP-2026-112 and flagged SRE + Eng for follow-up. support-bot: Ticket SUP-2026-112 created (priority: P2) :ticket:
support-bot: Linked request_id=req_0a1b2c to SUP-2026-112
Isha (Customer Success): Customer will try bypassing proxy and report back. They asked for recommended best-practice snippet we can send them to avoid this class of parse errors.
Alex P (Eng): Suggest snippet for customers: each SSE \"data:\" line must contain a complete JSON object or array item. Example: `data: {\"item\": {...}}\n` then final `data: {\"done\": true}`. Also recommend their parser incrementally parse each event rather than concatenating blindly.
Samir (SRE): I'll also add a short-term mitigation: if we see streaming responses to enterprise customers behind known proxy IPs, we can emit an explicit final event immediately before connection close (best-effort) so receivers get a termination marker when proxy closes badly. Not guaranteed but may reduce failures.
Maya (Support): Great. I'll update the ticket with repro steps, suggested snippets, and ask customer to test bypass. Please post any internal logs you find in the ticket. :thumbsup:
Isha (Customer Success): Thanks — passing along to Acme and will update here when they try bypass. :eyes:
